newsitem.title: USA: DC mayor signs bill to curb flight of businesses.
newsitem.headline: DC mayor signs bill to curb flight of businesses.

text.p: Attempting to stem the flight of businesses from the District of Columbia to its suburbs, D.C.'s mayor on Monday signed a tax bill designed to lower the cost of unemployment insurance for district employers, the city said Monday.

The new law reduces employers' taxable wage base from $10,000 to $9,000, the city said in a press statement. That means employers will be taxed for unemployment compensation on the first $9,000 paid during the year to each employee, instead of the current $10,000, the city said.
By comparison, Maryland's taxable wage base is $8,500 and Virginia's is $8,000, the mayor's office said.

Barry originally submitted the bill to D.C.'s 13-member council for review in December 1996, but no council member introduced the measure. "After persistent lobbying by the Mayor, the legislation was introduced and unanimously approved by the Council," the Mayor's office said.
In early 1997, the maximum weekly benefit rate will be cut from $359 to $309, the city said. Maryland's current maximum weekly benefit amount is $250, and Virginia's is $208, the city added.
"This measure will save an estimated $7l6 million in trust fund outlays during fiscal year 1997," the city said.
"This is the first measure of unemployment compensation tax relief to businesses in over 20 years," the city added.
